articles.title: Army invokes emergency powers to bypass court order and detonate lead in Iowa
articles.summary: By Jack Queen and Jim Urquhart AUGUSTA, Iowa, Nov 22 (Reuters) - The US Army will detonate 68 barrels of a toxic lead explosive in Iowa this week on emergency legal powers that allow it to bypass a court order blocking the controversial plan, the Trump administration told a court this ‌weekend. The US Court of Appeals for the 8th Circuit temporarily halted the detonation by freezing the Army's environmental permit on Thursday after environmental groups sued to ‌halt the operation. The government said in Saturday night's filing that the Army plans to move forward without a permit by invoking an emergency munitions and explosives exception to federal environmental protection laws. Federal officials say the ​detonation must go forward within the next several days because a drop in temperature could destabilize the material and cause an uncontrolled explosion. "The Army must perform a controlled detonation to protect the public from the more significant threat from an uncontrolled explosion," the Justice Department said in a court filing late on Saturday. The Army had previously postponed plans to detonate the degraded lead azide, an explosive used in military munitions, after public outcry by residents and farmers near Middletown, Iowa. The Justice Department said the Army would act by Tuesday, November ‌24. The Army later said in a post on ⁠X on Sunday the detonation would take place on Wednesday, November 25, "to allow for optimal weather conditions and all mitigation measures to be emplaced." The Army did not respond to a Reuters inquiry on Sunday about the precise timing of the detonation. "Additional details on this situation will ⁠be forthcoming," the Army said in its X post. DETAILS SOUGHT Lead exposure can cause serious health problems, particularly in children, including damage to the brain and nervous system. The Iowa Environmental Council and the Sierra Club's Iowa chapter filed the lawsuit challenging the detonation, arguing that the detonations would release a toxic plume of lead dust into the air that could travel 100 miles (160 km) ​north ​of the site, depending on weather conditions. Kerri Johannsen, senior director of policy and programs at the ​Iowa Environmental Council, told Reuters the Army should provide more details ‌about the timing of the detonation, where the plume is expected to travel, and what precautions people should take. “One of the pieces that especially raised our concerns was the lack of prior notice and the fact that many folks, including state officials, did not have any heads-up about this… There was not enough information being shared," Johannsen said. The Iowa Department of Agriculture and Land Stewardship has recommended that cattle farmers near the detonation site move their livestock, feed and equipment indoors or transport them to alternate locations. But farmers have told the environmental council that keeping livestock indoors is not a viable option, Johannsen said. In a statement on Thursday, acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle ‌said the Army had determined with the US Environmental Protection Agency that a controlled detonation ​to dispose of the degraded lead was the option that posed the lowest risk to the public. Still, ​the Army advised people to avoid the affected area during the detonation and ​urged anyone who could not leave beforehand to stay indoors, close windows and doors and shut off heating and cooling systems that ‌bring in outside air. Residents should wet-clean surfaces children may touch ​to remove any lead dust once the exposure ​period has ended, the Army said. “The early recommendations from the Army had a lot of people sort of with their jaws hanging open … There remain so many questions about mitigation and protection," Johannsen said. Jeremy Atwater, a resident of Augusta, Iowa, said he planned to head west because he expected the plume ​would blow south through his town. "Anything but the bomb," Atwater ‌told Reuters outside his home, as a set of two green swings in his yard swayed in the wind. "It's just going to be a ​big problem." (Reporting by Jack Queen in New York and Jim Urquhart in Augusta, Iowa; additional reporting by Ashraf Fahim in Washington and Luc Cohen ​in New York; Editing by Sergio Non, Bill Berkrot, Stephen Coates and Lincoln Feast.) articles.title: Army plans Tuesday detonation of 5 tons of explosives in Iowa as court fight continues
articles.summary: A sign sits on top of a building at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on Thursday in Middletown, Iowa. - Scott Olson/Getty Images The Justice Department on Sunday asked a federal appeals court to lift its pause on a permit allowing the US Army to detonate nearly five tons of material containing lead azide at an Iowa munitions plant. The Army intends to carry out the detonation Wednesday. A federal appeals court temporarily paused the US Environmental Protection Agency permit on Thursday that would allow the Army to detonate the material at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in tiny Middletown after environmental groups sued. The Army, in coordination with the EPA, plans to destroy nearly 70 drums containing lead azide, a compound used to detonate munitions, the military branch said. The detonation, originally scheduled for Friday morning, had been moved to Monday, and then Tuesday, before it was later moved to Wednesday. The Army said Sunday evening that it had moved the detonation to Wednesday “to allow for optimal weather conditions and all mitigation measures to be emplaced.” The Army’s plan has drawn heavy pushback from concerned Iowans and politicians about the plume’s spread over a vast swath of Iowa, the Mississippi River and into parts of Illinois. Environmental groups suing the EPA said the Army had, as of late Sunday morning, failed to update the public about latest weather forecasts, as well as projections of the path of the plume containing lead dust. Lead exposure is unhealthy at any level, and it’s especially dangerous to children, health officials said. The Army said Sunday evening that it was working to safeguard all Americans in the region. As the legal fight has unfolded, the Justice Department in a filing late Saturday said the court’s order “does not enjoin or otherwise prohibit the Army from acting under a separate legal authority.” The Army says the degraded material could explode on its own as temperatures drop. “The real choice, in other words, is not between a detonation and no detonation. It is between a planned and mitigated detonation and an unplanned and unmitigated explosion,” the filing said. Federal officials are now trying to bypass the judicial process and review while not showing they had pursued other safer alternatives than detonation, lawyers representing environmental groups argued. “People across numerous impacted communities speaking up and demanding accountability is the only reason there was an opportunity to pause and think about better ways to approach the lead azide problem,” Thien Chau, a senior attorney at Earthjustice, which represents the environmental groups, said in a statement Sunday. Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds on Friday activated a state emergency operations center, while officials in nearby Illinois are warning residents about dust spilling over into their state. The Federal Aviation Administration has restricted flights around Middletown from Monday through Wednesday, according to a temporary flight restriction notice . Here’s what we know about the planned detonation and the legal battle. Army says detonation is needed The Army in March , during “ routine stockpile surveillance,” discovered lead azide housed in bunkers had been degrading, according to Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle. Officials evaluating the best way to dispose of the material communicated with “stakeholders and the public in Middletown and the modeled impact area about the danger it posed,” Telle said. The lead azide’s degraded status left it “extremely unstable and sensitive to even slight friction or movement,” according to an FAQ distributed by the Army to the community last month. “Packing and transporting it poses an unacceptable risk of accidental detonation to personnel handling and transporting as well as to the public.” Completed shells ready for shipment on a train at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant assembly line in Middletown, Iowa, on January 26, 2023. - Lyndon French/The New York Times/Redux After coordinating with the EPA, experts and the community, officials “determined that a controlled detonation was the option that posed the lowest risk to the public in the immediate and surrounding area,” Telle said. Army officials held an October 15 community meeting to share information about a potential detonation in late November, according to documents on the plant’s page . Then, on November 15, the community got a notice of a detonation on Friday, according to an Army news release . After pushback, the Army rescheduled the detonation to Monday — the “latest possible moment prior to a forecasted temperature drop, which would risk further destabilization of the material,” Telle said. While noting the court’s pause is still in place, the City of Fort Madison said Saturday it was notified that the detonation would most likely occur either Monday or Tuesday, but if it doesn’t happen this week, “another time will need to be arranged with additional planning.” City officials said they hadn’t been given any further information but expect the state to issue more details on Sunday. Waiting too long to detonate the lead azide could pose more hazards later, Telle said. The emergency permit from the EPA would allow the Army to do the detonation between November 13 and February 11, 2027. unknown content item - Still, the problem should have been evaluated 20 years ago, said Patrick O’Shaughnessy, a University of Iowa professor and environmental health expert. “Somebody left it to rot that long, for it to now being the only option is to blow it up on site because it can’t be moved,” he told CNN. O’Shaughnessy said the situation is “unprecedented” and called a planned detonation “the lesser of two evils.” “They’re pretty much up against a wall here to get it done,” he told CNN’s Jessica Dean on Sunday. The Army had previously awarded a contract to MuniRem Environmental, a Georgia-based firm that uses chemicals to neutralize munitions, but later canceled the deal citing safety concerns, court filings show, and instead opted to detonate the lead azide. The filings were first reported by The New York Times. “This decision is supported by the technical consensus across military and federal explosive safety authorities that this is the only safe method of treatment,” read a partially redacted September letter included in the court filings from Amy L. Borman, deputy assistant secretary of the Army for Environment, Safety and Occupational Health. CNN has reached out to the Army for comment. Valentine Nzengung, a chief executive at MuniRem, told CNN the Army “told us that they evaluated reports and they found out that controlled detonation was the safest way, and that is why they were moving forward with controlled detonation. They did not provide us much more detail than this.” Iowans and local officials push back Officials at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant have regularly updated officials in Middletown – home to 363 people – about the planned detonation, according to Brieanna Beck, the city clerk and municipal officer, who said she has quickly shared each update on the city’s Facebook page. The city has been aware of the detonation plan for a couple of months, she told CNN in an email. The Army plant sent letters to homes potentially affected by the detonation, Beck said. Shells are seen getting their final capping on the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant assembly line, in Middletown, Iowa, on January 26, 2023. - Lyndon French/The New York Times/Redux The governor’s office and state agencies were coordinating with EPA and Army officials to “continuously monitor the situation and keep local partners informed,” Reynolds said Friday. More than 80 miles north of Middletown, Cedar Rapids is preparing for the detonation. Officials in Iowa’s second-most populous city are taking steps to monitor the drinking water supply — drawn from wells along the Cedar River — for potential contamination, though they don’t anticipate impacts, according to a city update . But plans and communication around the detonation have gotten strong pushback from environmental advocates, as well as state and federal politicians in Iowa and neighboring Illinois. Officials in Iowa City, about 60 miles north of Middletown, said they didn’t know about the planned detonation until news began circulating early last week and were unaware of any state or federal agency formally notifying them, according to City Manager Geoff Fruin in a declaration on Saturday supporting the environmental groups’ lawsuit. An email Friday told the city an EPA team was deployed to collect a pre-detonation surface water sample because Iowa City, with a population of over 75,000 people, is within a 100-mile radius of the detonation, he said. Iowa City officials have been discussing possible protocols to address impacts from the detonation, Fruin said. But he added it’s difficult to plan due to “lack of notice and information.” Josh Turek, the US senator-elect for Iowa, has called for a delay to the detonation and Rob Sand, the incoming governor, said Iowans’ safety now and in the future should be the government’s top concern. Parts of western and central Illinois could be affected by the lead plume under the current weather forecast, Illinois state officials said in an update Friday. Illinois health and environmental protection officials said they are monitoring the planned detonation and have issued updates to residents. Illinois agriculture officials have issued guidance to protect livestock and pets, recommending keeping animals inside until the plume has passed and warning of exposure through fishing. Residents should stay indoors on the detonation day, with windows and doors closed for one to two days after as a precaution, Illinois officials said. They also encouraged people to use portable air cleaners equipped with a HEPA filter. Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker said Friday he had spoken with Telle, urging more transparency about the planned detonation. What the court has said Environmental advocates sued the US EPA on Thursday over the emergency permit allowing the Army to detonate the lead azide, citing concerns about the potential impacts of the explosion. The Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals on Thursday temporarily stayed the EPA’s emergency permit until it rules on the groups’ emergency motion, but didn’t say when the court would take action on the case. The Army, in a joint statement with the US Department of Health and Human Services and the EPA, said Friday afternoon, “The entire interagency is working together to ensure that the controlled detonation in Middletown, Iowa, is conducted in the safest fashion possible.” “Officials have been meticulously planning for this event since March, and all agencies involved are prepared to take the most extreme mitigation measures available to ensure there is no risk to the public and any disruptions are minimized,” the statement said, adding they will keep local officials and the public updated. The cleanup requirements under the current permit are inadequate to properly address the scope and degree of potential impacts, according to Chau, the senior attorney at Earthjustice, who filed the lawsuit on behalf of the Iowa Environmental Council and the Sierra Club Iowa Chapter. There doesn’t appear to be sufficient understanding of how far the plume would spread, as well as which bodies of water, such as the Mississippi River, and land would be blanketed with lead dust, including where people live, Chau told reporters Friday. A sign welcomes travelers to town on November 19 in Middletown, Iowa. The town sits near the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant and is in danger of lead exposure from a planned detonation of tainted ordinance. - Scott Olson/Getty Images The Justice Department first cited a federal regulation that exempts responses to an “immediate threat” to human health, public safety, property or the environment from EPA permitting requirements in its Friday filing. In Saturday’s filing, it said the Army intends to invoke that exemption. Col. Aaron Teller, commander of the Army’s 71st Ordnance Group, which handles explosive ordnance disposal, determined the lead azide poses “an immediate threat,” according to a sworn declaration filed with Saturday’s notice. The Justice Department has not responded to CNN’s request for comment. “We want to be absolutely clear that the regulation they cite is an extraordinary and extreme backstop for situations where there is truly nothing else that can be done,” Rachel Rintelmann, a managing attorney at Earthjustice, said in an email of the Friday filing. Federal courts have the authority to prohibit the detonation, said Richard Revesz, a New York University School of Law professor who specializes in environmental and regulatory law and was an Office of Management and Budget official during the Biden administration. Courts should carefully consider whether the Army is correct in its assertion that controlled detonation was the “option that posed the lowest risk to the public in the immediate and surrounding area,” Revesz said in an email to CNN, citing Telle’s statement on the detonation . Health risks of lead exposure There is no safe level of lead in the body, Dr. Sameer Vohra, director of the Illinois Department of Public Health, said in a statement . “(And) when inhaled or swallowed, it can pose serious health risks.” unknown content item - With the detonation, the hope is if the lead azide spreads over a wider area, it won’t stay in high-level concentrations, according to O’Shaughnessy, the University of Iowa professor. “It’s kind of like one of these, the solution to pollution is dilution, right?” he said. There is the potential for exposure through the air during the initial plume or through touch after it has settled, he said. Lead is toxic to the brain. Exposure is known to cause serious harm to children’s health, resulting in slowed growth and development, as well as problems with learning, behavior, hearing and speech, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention . Environmental advocates also warn the detonation could worsen health for residents in Iowa, which has the second-highest rate of cancer of any US state and is one of only three states where the rate is rising. CNN’s Holly Yan, Kara Devlin and Bill Kirkos contributed to this report. articles.title: Iranian attacks in Strait of Hormuz hit highest levels since war began
articles.summary: A liquefied petroleum gas tanker burning in the Strait of Hormuz off the Musandam Peninsula, Oman, on Tuesday. - Lewis Pugh Foundation/AP Reported attacks on shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz are at the highest levels since the Iran war began, maritime data shows, as Tehran seeks to re-exert its control over the critical waterway amid falling oil prices. In October, the number of attacks reported to the Royal Navy-affiliated United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre (UKMTO) exceeded 30 for the first time since the US-Iran war began in late February. As of Sunday, at least 22 attacks were reported in November, the second highest figure since the war began, according to a CNN analysis of UKMTO data. The reporting area covers the Strait of Hormuz, the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman. The numbers from the UK maritime monitor are likely an undercount since the organization only reports incidents verified through primary sources. “Additional incidents are known but cannot be independently verified,” UKMTO said in its weekly overview published on Friday. As attacks on ships in the strategic waterway have stepped up in recent months, many are believed to have switched off their commercial tracking devices to avoid detection. In a report released in mid October the organization said it was “struggling to accurately report true number of attacks with majority of vessels attacked refusing to report to UKMTO.” Meanwhile, Iran’s military has claimed near-daily incidents involving commercial ships transiting through the strait, often attributing them to sea mines rather than drone or missile attacks. Before October, the number of reported attacks in the region averaged around 10 per month. Numbers vary, but data from the International Maritime Organization also points to October as having the highest number of confirmed incidents so far this year. Since the conflict began, the strait has become a heavily contested frontier , with attacks there disrupting oil and gas shipping and sparking global economic fallout. Iran began trying to halt traffic in the wake of the US-Israeli attacks that launched the war. In response, the US imposed a blockade on Iranian ports, and as CNN previously reported , Gulf producers have found ways of getting ships through the strait. Commercial traffic through the channel – through which a fifth of the world’s oil passed before the war – remains at a reduced level when compared to the 2025 baseline. As global oil prices fall and the Iran’s domestic crude revenues come under increasing strain, Tehran has been stepping up attacks, with experts saying the country is losing its leverage over the waterway and could escalate attacks further in an attempt to force concessions from Washington. No need for a deal, Trump says The International Energy Agency attributes the recent decline in oil prices to a recovery in Gulf exports. Prices also fell after the US midterm results as concerns over fresh US military action in the Middle East subsided. “Markets appear to be increasingly assuming that a return to full-scale war is unlikely and that oil supplies will gradually recover,” Hamidreza Azizi, a senior Iran analyst at the International Crisis Group (ICG) think tank, told CNN . “But that assumption could change quickly if Iran decides to intensify the confrontation.” A man pumps fuel at a gas station in Miami, Florida, on November 10. - Joe Raedle/Getty Images Meanwhile, Iran’s domestic oil revenues are falling sharply as the US blockade of Iranian ports continues to stifle the country’s supply of oil to global markets, according to maritime data tracking service Kpler. “Iranian oil on water outside the (US) blockade zone has hit zero as the last cargoes discharged in China earlier this month. Consequently, Iran’s oil revenues could drop to zero by mid-December,” Kpler reported in late October. US President Donald Trump said this month the US doesn’t “need a deal” with Tehran and ordered Vice President JD Vance to turn his focus elsewhere . “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed!” Trump posted on Truth Social. “We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” He later indicated he wouldn’t hesitate to resume military strikes in Iran if necessary. Three tankers struck in Hormuz since Friday During the latest attacks, projectiles struck three tankers exiting the strait on Friday and Saturday, according to Marisks, a maritime risk management company. Marisks did not confirm who was behind the attacks, though it said Iranian involvement was “assessed as likely.” Fire erupted aboard the Captain Leon, a Marshall Islands-flagged chemical and oil tanker, after it was struck at the bow at 3 p.m. UTC (10 a.m. ET) on Friday. All crew were reported safe, Marisks said. The Torkel, a Hong Kong-flagged crude oil tanker, caught fire after being hit in the stern at 5 a.m. UTC on Saturday (midnight ET on Saturday). Less than an hour later, the Arina, also Hong Kong-flagged, was struck in the engine room by a missile. The attacks demonstrate the “continued critical threat” to commercial shipping in the region, Marisks said, particularly through the “southern corridor” near Oman’s coastline which Iran vehemently opposes. CNN’s Eleni Giokos, Laura Sharman, Nadeen Ebrahim and Alayna Treene contributed reporting. articles.title: Jon Ossoff's decisive Senate win in Georgia fuels presidential buzz
articles.summary: Washington — Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff's commanding reelection victory in Georgia is drawing renewed attention to his potential as a 2028 presidential contender, as election data shows how he assembled a broad coalition of voters in the pivotal presidential battleground state. Despite the growing speculation, Ossoff, 39, is for now dismissing the possibility of a White House bid. During a debate in October, Ossoff said he had "zero interest in running for president" in 2028. Some early polls place him at the top of a hypothetical 2028 primary field. A post-election Emerson College survey showed Ossoff with the support of 17% of respondents — narrowly ahead of former Vice President Kamala Harris and New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, with former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg and California Gov. Gavin Newsom rounding out the top five. Ossoff has attracted interest from both centrists and progressives while delivering a decisive victory in a closely divided presidential battleground state. At Crooked Con, a primarily progressive gathering in Washington after the midterms, Ossoff received 38% of first-choice votes in its straw poll, ahead of Ocasio-Cortez and Buttigieg. "I think he would make an attractive presidential contender on the Democratic side," said Jerry Gonzalez, CEO of GALEO Impact Fund PAC, a Georgia-based Latino political action committee that endorsed Ossoff in his Senate race. "He is not afraid, he won't shy away from holding the Trump administration accountable, but in a way that works towards actually building coalitions to get something done." Democrats who can win statewide in conservative or swing states tend to be moderate, and that's true of Ossoff, too. "He comes across, and tries to present himself, as a moderate, and he talks about issues which moderate conservatives could get behind," said Charles Bullock, a longtime political science professor at the University of Georgia. "The issues he stresses are things which are within the broad mainstream of 'These would be good things.'" It's unclear how well a moderate would fare in the early nominating states. What is effective in a Georgia general election may be a tougher sell in a Democratic primary, where voters often reward ideological purity over swing-state caution. "Obviously, he's successful here in Georgia," Bullock said. "How would he play elsewhere? "I think what we will be seeing is preparation, maybe for a later run," Bullock speculated. Ossoff's record gives rivals on both flanks openings to attack: progressives have criticized his vote for the Republican-backed Laken Riley Act and his reluctance to embrace "Medicare for All," while his votes to restrict certain weapons sales to Israel and his criticism of its military conduct in Gaza have drawn objections from some pro-Israel Democrats and donors. All of those issues are certain to be part of the 2028 primary contest. For example, Rep. Ro Khanna, another potential 2028 candidate, last week tried to restart the debate over universal healthcare. "Medicare for All means healthcare for everyone, like public school is free for every kid," Khanna wrote on X, arguing, "'Medicare for All who want it' is pablum. It's telling parents they have to pay for public school." In his reelection this month, Ossoff defeated GOP opponent Mike Collins by around 18 points, two years after President Trump defeated Harris by around two points in 2024. It was a much wider margin than his last Senate election, which he won by just over one percentage point. Powering Ossoff's win this year was a broad coalition of voters, including some swing constituencies that Democrats have struggled with in recent years, CBS News' exit polling shows. Ossoff maintained strong support among Black voters, winning 93% of the group, which make up almost one-third of the state's eligible voters according to Pew Research Center . He did not win the White voters who make up just over half of Georgia's electorate, but he did make significant inroads, winning 40% — after Harris had won just 28% two years earlier. He also notched some improvement in groups that have shifted hard against Democrats: He won 29% of White voters without college degrees (compared to Harris' 18%) and 19% of White evangelical or born-again Christian voters (compared to less than 10% for Harris). Ossoff also won men by nine points after Harris lost them by 13 points. Both Ossoff and Harris won younger Georgians, but Ossoff won them by a larger margin, securing 85% of voters ages 29 and under. Ossoff also split the 45-and-older vote roughly in half, while Harris lost that age group by a 15-point margin. And Ossoff made gains with Hispanics — a group that makes up less than 10% of Georgia's eligible voters but which has grown rapidly and has become a swing demographic that could decide a close race in the perennial battleground. In his reelection victory, he won around two-thirds of Latino voters, up seven points from Harris' performance two years earlier. A comparison of 19 Georgia precincts where at least 30% of active registered voters identify as Hispanic or Latino shows substantial Democratic improvement. Ossoff won those precincts by a combined 49 points in the two-candidate vote, compared with an eight-point advantage for Harris in the 2024 presidential election and an 18-point margin for fellow Democratic Sen. Raphael Warnock in 2022. The changes were significant in areas that had supported Mr. Trump just two years earlier. In six heavily Latino precincts in Whitfield County, the combined results shifted from a 12-point Trump advantage in 2024 to a 37-point Ossoff victory in 2026. Three similar precincts in Hall County shifted from an 11-point Trump edge to a 33-point Ossoff victory. Those figures reflect the voting behavior of entire precincts rather than individual Latino voters, and comparisons between presidential and midterm electorates are not exact. Still, they underscore how dramatically the environment changed in places with large Latino populations. Gonzalez attributed the shift in part to concerns over affordability and immigration enforcement, two issues he said weighed heavily on Latino voters in Georgia. "Things are really expensive," Gonzalez told CBS News. "The price and affordability were a big driving issue." He also pointed to the Trump administration's immigration crackdown and its impact on Latino communities in Georgia. Ossoff has investigated allegations of abuses in federal immigration detention facilities as part of his Senate oversight work. Gonzalez also credited Ossoff's success among voters across the political spectrum to his accessibility and constituent outreach. "His office is accessible to all Georgians, and that's part of the reason why he won." In this wave election, Ossoff wasn't the only Democrat to pick up ground in the midterms. Latino and Black voters, men, voters without college degrees and younger voters moved back toward Democratic candidates nationwide, a reversal after all four groups had shifted rightward in 2024. In 2028, those groups could once again play a central role in both the Democratic Party's nominating process and the general election. States with large Black and Latino populations will lead the Democratic primary calendar after the party rearranged its schedule, and Ossoff, with his strong support from both groups, would likely stand to benefit if he were to decide to run. South Carolina — where Black Democratic voters have long played an influential role in choosing the party's presidential nominee — will go first, followed by Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan and Virginia. The DNC says approximately 4.2 million Latinos live across the six early nominating states, a major increase from the party's previous early-state lineup. In the general election, maintaining a strong lead with Black, Latino and younger voters — and preventing too much slippage among White and non-college-educated voters — will also be a core task for Democrats, as they seek to prevent the GOP's first non-Trump presidential candidate in over a decade from reassembling the Trump coalition. Though Ossoff says he doesn't plan a White House bid in 2028, his performance in Georgia has provided an early measure of what an electoral coalition for him could look like. "He has mentioned that he was focused on winning reelection, which he has done, so I think that gives him a little bit of latitude to think about it a little more seriously," Gonzalez said. articles.title: ICE arrests by masked agents at Seattle airport enrage passengers and state officials
articles.summary: Screams rang out on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle as two masked, plainclothes federal immigration officers detained a father and daughter as they boarded a flight bound for Los Angeles. The daughter, identified by authorities as Sofia Hernandez Mejia, clung to an agent’s leg as she pleaded: “Please, I beg you, I beg you, I beg you, no.” “They’re taking my dad. ... We have a work permit,” she told fellow passengers. “I’m being arrested by ICE.” The Immigration and Customs Enforcement arrests at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport , captured on multiple videos on Saturday morning and shared on social media, enraged state and local leaders, immigrant advocates and passengers who witnessed them. ICE has increased arrests at airports over the last year, including of foreign citizens with expired U.S. visas. “ICE is completely and totally out of control,” Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson wrote on X . “Like many Americans, I’m outraged by masked agents, who do not identify themselves, dragging people off jetways as they board a flight.” The Department of Homeland Security responded to the governor’s remarks, posting on X that officers had been targeting Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, a Mexican national who overstayed his visa. During the arrest, the agency said Hernandez “hurled hot coffee on the officers.” The officers arrested Hernandez, who they said also overstayed her visa, and said she would be charged with assaulting a federal officer. In videos of the arrests, one officer appeared to have a stain on his jacket. A passenger seemingly contested that allegation, with one heard telling an officer: “She didn’t throw coffee on you, bro.” The Associated Press reported that the family was headed to California for a baptism ceremony, according to their lawyer, Olia Catala. In a post on Instagram, Catala said her clients have no criminal history and “are pursuing their immigration cases through the proper legal process.” John Gaedeke, a passenger on the flight, told The Times that the plane was half loaded when he spotted the two men — who he later learned were officers — cutting the line. Gaedeke said he heard the men whisper to each other, “Should we do it? There he is, let’s go.” Soon after, Gaedeke said he saw the officers tackle a man, and “then it just turned to chaos.” People cried as they filmed, he said, and Alaska Airlines staff were “in a state of shock.” A woman standing in front of him with her young son turned her body to protect him. “She was obviously scared. Her son was petrified,” Gaedeke said, describing what unfolded as “theatrical violence.” “The instant grief from the family members, just the screaming, crying and wailing — that still sticks with me.” Gaedeke said it didn’t look to him like the coffee was thrown at the agents. In his Instagram caption, he described the incident as “the most f— up thing I have personally witnessed in this country.” The Port of Seattle, which operates the airport, said in a statement that immigration enforcement actions are conducted “without the Port’s participation or knowledge.” Port officials said they were “outraged” by what occurred and were in conversation with Homeland Security on whether protocols “were breached.” “This incident was not only distressing for the affected family but the passengers around them, and Port officials continue to engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred,” the statement read. Alaska Airlines said in a statement that it was “concerned” by what unfolded “during the boarding of Alaska Flight 1306.” The airline said it was not provided advance notice of the enforcement action, “and we are working to understand the circumstances surrounding what occurred, including whether the proper protocols were followed.” “We recognize how distressing this incident has been for employees and guests,” they said. A GoFundMe launched for the father and daughter, which had raised more than $40,000 by Sunday morning, described the family as “very grateful for all the love and support that they have received so far from family, friends, and community leaders and members.” “Legal proceedings and the following events can be drawn out long-term and become very costly,” Yareli Farias, who described herself as a close friend of the family, wrote on GoFundMe. “The funds raised will be used for legal expenses related to this case.” In a Saturday afternoon news conference, Katie Garrow, executive secretary-treasurer of MLK Labor, which represents thousands of unionized workers at the airport, said they were alerted to the arrests by flight attendants. “They are the ones who rang the alarm that this escalation broke protocol and crossed a red line,” Garrow said. Garrow said the incident was “so disturbing and upsetting to workers” that four of the six crew members on Flight 1306 “chose not to fly” that morning. At the news conference, Ferguson called video of the arrests “horrific” and “chilling.” He described it as “the latest example of the violence that ICE has inflicted on our communities as it works to further Donald Trump’s cruel immigration agenda.” “There is no justification for this brutality,” the governor said. Ferguson said he will request that every airline in the airport call on ICE “to get out of our airports.” “We need a system of immigration enforcement and border security that is effective, ethical and humane. And ICE is not it,” he said. “It is beyond reform. ... It is time to abolish Donald Trump’s ICE.” Times staff writer Matthew Ormseth contributed to this report. articles.title: Rep. Virginia Foxx loses reelection bid after 11 terms in North Carolina
articles.summary: Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx has been officially unseated by Democratic challenger Chuck Hubbard in North Carolina after a recount — requested by Foxx — broke in Hubbard’s favor. The Associated Press called the election for Hubbard early Sunday afternoon. Hubbard, who lost to Foxx by 19 points two years ago, said in a statement that the incumbent had "graciously conceded." "Let me be the first to thank Congresswoman Foxx for her decades of service and countless sacrifices," Hubbard wrote on social media. "I deeply appreciate her commitment to a smooth transition of the office and constituent casework. We may not always agree, but we both love North Carolina and the people of the Fifth District." Hubbard's win marks the seventh seat Democrats flipped in the state this year despite Republican redistricting efforts last year. North Carolina will send 11 Democrats and three Republicans to Congress — a reversal of the 10-4 Republican majority voters elected in 2024. The Democratic win also notches the broader party an election-year record: Having secured 258 seats, the Democrats have won their largest share of House seats in a national election since the early '90s. Foxx had requested the recount in a letter to election officials on Nov. 17, when the margin between the two candidates was 331 votes. In her letter to the State Board of Election, Foxx cited a state law that allows candidates to request a recount when the margin of victory is less than 1 percent. Foxx was first elected in 2004. Now 83, she is finishing her 11th term and has already filed paperwork to run in the 2028 race. articles.title: Israeli settlers launch attacks in West Bank as Netanyahu rival decries 'Jewish terrorism'
articles.summary: Israeli settlers launched a series of attacks across the occupied West Bank, torching at least a dozen cars and vandalizing several homes overnight Sunday, in what Gadi Eisenkot , the main rival of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, decried as “Jewish terrorism.” Video from the village of Kufr Malik, about 10 miles northeast of Ramallah, the seat of the Palestinian Authority in the West Bank, showed several cars in flames with thick smoke pouring into the sky as a siren blares in the background. In the same village, a home was tagged with Hebrew graffiti, including the word “revenge.” Similar scenes unfolded in the nearby villages of Deir as-Sudan and Deir Abu Masha’al, two Palestinian communities northwest of Ramallah that were also attacked by settlers. Mustafa Barghouti, the president of the Palestinian National Initiative, said the brazen attacks were part of an escalating pattern of settler violence. unknown content item - “Palestinian families are facing violence, destruction and the loss of their homes,” he said on X. Eisenkot said the violence was the result of the policies of pro-settler, far-right politicians Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, who he said “brought the area to the brink of anarchy.” Smotrich was the key architect of a massive expansion of Israeli settlements and outposts in the West Bank over the last four years, while Ben-Gvir has been accused of turning a blind eye to settler violence. Eisenkot said the attacks were “acts of Jewish terrorism, and we must call them by their name.” Eisenkot, who has four more weeks to attempt to form a government and oust Netanyahu, said the Israeli government should use administrative detention and targeted operations against the assailants. A Palestinian man inspects a damaged car, which Palestinians say were burned by Israeli settlers, in Kafr Malik, near Ramallah. - Mohamad Torokman/Reuters Netanyahu has not issued any public statement about the attacks. CNN has reached out to his office for comment. Netanyahu has repeatedly tried to downplay settler violence, previously saying it was the result of what he has called “juvenile delinquents.” The West Bank has seen a surge in settler violence in recent months, particularly around the annual olive harvest, where Palestinians have repeatedly been harassed and attacked. There have been 410 settler attacks related to the olive harvest since the beginning of September, according to the UN. This weekend’s attacks occurred across several locations in the middle of the night. There were no reports of injuries. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said it also received reports of an attack on the Palestinian village of At-Turwani in the southern West Bank near the city of Hebron. The IDF said in a statement it “condemns acts of violence of this nature, which harm public order.” Israeli police said on Sunday they would enter the Palestinian villages under IDF escort to collect evidence. Police have not announced any arrests after the attacks. “Settler terrorism in the West Bank does not take place in a vacuum,” said Yousef Jabareen, the chair of the Arab Joint List party, which saw a surge in support in recent elections. “It is the direct result of the deepening occupation and a government policy under which violence against Palestinians has become an everyday occurrence.” The attacks on Palestinian villages and sites have not been limited to the West Bank. On Thursday morning, a mosque in northern Israel was torched and vandalized with graffiti similar to the messages sprayed across Palestinian homes in the West Bank. Pictures shared by Arab lawmaker Ahmad Tibi showed the inside of the mosque burned and charred. He blamed anti-Arab rhetoric and “people who were poisoned by Netanyahu’s incitement” for the arson. “The police and the Shin Bet must get to the perpetrators. And immediately,” he said on X. Zeena Saifi contributed reporting. articles.title: World's longest climate summit ends without a deal after fossil fuel dispute
articles.summary: The Cop31 climate summit in Turkey descended into disarray and disappointment after countries were unable to reach consensus on a deal that failed to mention fossil fuels. Nations rejected the agreement at a fraught closing session in Antalya on Sunday, almost two days after the summit was due to finish in what stretched to become the longest Cop in history. The European Union , the UK and small island states such as Tuvalu refused to accept the text over the absence of references to fossil fuels, blasting the omissions as “greenwashing” and accusing oil states of “hijacking” the talks. Ireland’s minister for climate Darragh O’Brien, speaking on behalf of the EU, called the text “unconscionable” and said its ambition went “nowhere near the level of action that's required to deal with climate change”. A spokesperson for the British delegation said it was “profoundly disappointed” by the proposed deal. Some nations indicated a willingness to continue working, but at the closing plenary summit president ⁠Murat ​Kurum said ⁠there would be no new ⁠draft of the ​deal. COP31 president Murat Kurum leaves after the final plenary session on the second overtime day on Sunday (Getty) Andy Burnham was the only G7 leader to attend the summit, where he made an impassioned speech promising to usher in a “new era of British leadership" on climate change. But the prime minister said nothing on Sunday as hopes of a deal evaporated and delegates eventually left empty handed. UK energy secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh later called the failure to reach a deal “immensely disappointing”, but said there had been “genuine progress” during the conference. “This Cop sought to confront hard truths – that global warming is set to overshoot 1.5C and that we must act with ever more urgency to address it,” she said in a statement. “The moment required bold ambition and we have been working tirelessly to try to build consensus. It is immensely disappointing we have been unable to do so.” The failed deal had acknowledged the planet's projected temperature overshoot for the first time and called for faster development of carbon-removal technologies to eventually reverse it. It was already heavily criticised by small islands and civil society groups who called it a “betrayal” and criticised its reliance on carbon capture schemes, which had been pushed by oil states including Saudi Arabia. "It seems like we are negotiating with the Saudis," Maina Talia, Tuvalu's climate minister, commented during the conference. A representative for the Saudi delegation, which supported the deal's mention of carbon removal, told the summit he was surprised at the ‌resistance to technology, which he said offered a “concrete solution”. Ireland's minister for climate, environment, energy and transport Darragh O'Brien (L) had criticised the draft deal (AFP/Getty) Developing countries had also criticised the deal for not providing sufficient new funds to ​help them adapt to a warming planet. China and India said they had objections but chose to accept the cover text to move things forward. The Cop process is the main vehicle through which countries coordinate efforts to curb global warming. Its annual meeting provides an opportunity for nations to signal they are willing to work together to find solutions and help finance the problems rising temperatures cause. Earlier, Mr Kurum, defended the text and said the presidencies had “listened to everyone” and tried to bring the groups together, but admitted there was “no consensus”. Despite a failure to strike a deal, Mr Kurum said the summit had come to smaller agreements on plans to scale up global geothermal energy supply by 2050, build greener freight corridors and increase the electricity share of global energy to 35% by 2035. Australia's Cop31 president of negotiations, Chris Bowen, called the outcome "very disappointing" and said disagreements over fuels ​and ⁠climate finance were the dealbreakers. The conference became the longest COP ever on Sunday afternoon, passing COP25 in Madrid in 2019, which ran 44 hours over its schedule. Delegates pored over several drafts with language that tried to bridge the position of countries most exposed to climate impacts and those whose economies depend on producing or consuming fossil fuels, but the split came down to whether the text should refer to oil, gas and coal at all. The first time the transition away from fossil fuels found a mention in a UN climate agreement was at Cop28 in Dubai in 2023. It had been hoped that a series of climate disasters in the lead up to this year’s conference would help to sharpen minds and reaffirm commitments. The last time UN climate talks failed to get a deal adopted by all was in Copenhagen in 2009. Chief executive of environmental charity Friends of the Earth Asad Rehman said the deal in its current form “is no deal at all” and urged governments to pledge more than “wooly” promises. He warned leaders the “clock is ticking” and said governments must “come back to the negotiating table ready to deliver”. United Nations secretary-general Antonio Guterres also said he was "deeply disappointed” by the conference’s failure to reach a consensus. “I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands,” he said. "There may be no consensus in the negotiating room. There is no ambiguity in the science." Some campaigners also turned on the EU, which rejected the text while some lauded the resistance shown at the plenary. "The EU is trying to shift blame onto others and it is deeply hypocritical. At the beginning of COP31, it signalled it was prepared to drop the renewables ask from the electrification target and it has failed to put forward an EU fossil fuel transition roadmap," said Laurie van der Burg of Oil Change International. The failure is a blow to efforts to ratchet up international ‌action, but does not erase the obligations agreed by previous ‌summits or remove existing agreements on action against climate change. articles.title: NYC releases 84,000 more 9/11 records as portal tops 11 million visits
articles.summary: The Tribute in Light is illuminated on the skyline of lower Manhattan in New York City on Sept. 11, 2024. (LEONARDO MUNOZ/Getty Images) New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's administration released 84,000 more records Sunday on the city's response to the Sept. 11 attacks, pushing its public portal past 440,000 pages as unique visits topped 11 million. The batch is the third installment under a settlement with 9/11 Health Watch, an advocacy group created by the New York State AFL-CIO, and City Hall said more records will follow in the coming months. Mamdani's fiscal 2027 budget sets aside $34 million to build and maintain the portal. "More than 11 million visits and 440,000 pages later, our work is not finished," Mamdani said in a statement . Manhattan Borough President Brad Hoylman-Sigal framed each release as a step toward answering when City Hall learned the air at ground zero could make people sick. The city counts its releases in records but measures the archive in pages. An October installment of 40,000 records lifted the total to more than 200,000 pages, up from roughly 170,000 at the portal's September launch . That first release included the so-called Harding Memo, an undated letter to Robert Harding, a deputy mayor under former Mayor Rudy Giuliani, that listed potential grounds for lawsuits against the city, including health advisories that sent people back into the area too soon. It also included the "68 boxes" of Department of Environmental Protection files that the city said went unlocated until 2025 despite repeated requests under the state's public records law. The releases have drawn pushback from Giuliani's camp. His spokesman, Ted Goodman, accused Mamdani in September of trying to score political points by blaming local officials rather than radical Islam, and Giuliani said the terrorists bore full responsibility while faulting the Environmental Protection Agency for declaring air samples safe, NBC New York reported . The disclosures followed a courtroom loss for the city. In a May 28 decision, Justice James G. Clynes of the New York State Supreme Court in Manhattan, the state's trial-level court, found the department had acted "arbitrarily and capriciously," meaning without a reasonable basis, in denying the group's records request, according to the settlement signed Sept. 2. The deal requires monthly meetings for a year to review how many documents and pages the city has posted, plus a log of records it located but withheld. Separately, the city's Department of Investigation, its internal watchdog agency, is examining what officials knew about post-9/11 air quality and when they knew it, in an inquiry mandated by the City Council, amNY reported . © 2026 Newsmax. articles.title: Bay Area residents urged to avoid Thanksgiving travel as extreme flooding looms
articles.summary: Caltrans employees work to unclog drains in floodwater near Highway 101 freeway in San Francisco on Wednesday. (Benjamin Fanjoy / Getty Images) The California coast could see all-time-high sea levels this week, with officials warning of the potential for major seawater flooding of coastal neighborhoods. The San Francisco Bay Area faces an added threat because a strong storm will strike the region just as the highest tides so far this year arrive. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie urged residents to avoid unnecessary travel, with the city still reeling from exceptional flooding from last week’s powerful rainstorm. Problems are also likely on the Southern California coast, where sea levels could be even higher than on Oct. 27, when records were shattered and homes and businesses were flooded in  cities including Huntington Beach, Newport Beach, Long Beach, Redondo Beach and San Diego. The dangerous weather is being fueled by El Niño, hot ocean temperatures and unusually powerful king tides that are among the highest in two decades. Unlike Southern California, Northern California will also see a moderate-to-heavy rainstorm starting Tuesday, expected to whip up larger breaking waves and add to the potential for flooding. Even San Francisco International Airport and Oakland San Francisco Bay Airport are at risk of flooding, according to meteorologist Anamaria Navarrete of the National Weather Service’s Monterey office, which warned of “extreme coastal flooding” along the San Francisco Bay shoreline. “San Francisco could face a combination of exceptionally high tides, heavy rain and strong winds over the coming days,” the mayor said in a video posted on social media. “And our waterfront is expecting king tides, which are anticipated to bring the highest tide levels in San Francisco’s history. “This is a warning that I want everybody to take seriously. We want you to avoid unnecessary travel, especially around these peak tide periods that are coming,” Lurie said. The San Francisco Department of Emergency Management suggested avoiding unnecessary travel starting Monday afternoon through Wednesday; Marin County officials urged the same between 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Tuesday through Thanksgiving Day, especially in flood-prone areas. Crews were rushing to install emergency flood barriers along the bay shoreline, including at the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge toll plaza, where a “ Tiger Dam ” was installed. State transportation officials ordered the shutdown of the only vehicular route out of western Alameda to Oakland — the Posey Tube tunnel — starting Sunday night. And Marin County said people on the entire Tiburon Peninsula should consider leaving low-lying areas before the daily highest tide, starting Sunday through Black Friday, due to the flood risk. A motorist tries to navigate the 2300 block of Willow Street in Long Beach after heavy rains flooded the area on Thursday. (Allen J. Schaben/Los Angeles Times) Set during the most powerful El Niño on record — and during a confluence of extremely high tides and a big storm — the all-time maximum sea level at the San Francisco tidal gauge at Crissy Field was set on Jan. 27, 1983, at 8.66 feet above the baseline (currently defined as the average daily lowest-water level observed between 1983 and 2001). As of Saturday morning, the prediction for the maximum sea level this week was 8.8 feet, but by Sunday morning, the prediction was adjusted downward to 8.6 feet. It’s still possible that sea levels could exceed 9 feet. “That is all dependent on how much storm surge that we get,” Navarrete said Saturday evening. “We can guarantee that we’ll have at least a foot to a foot and a half due to thermal expansion because of our warmer waters,” but it’s the level of storm surge that comes with the storm that’ll determine “if we are going to break records.” “Places that have rarely, or never, flooded before may be inundated,” UC Agriculture and Natural Resources climate scientist Daniel Swain said . It’s not rain falling from the sky that’s the main threat; it’s areas at risk of saltwater flooding from the ocean or the bay, he added. The rain itself isn’t expected to be as intense as last week’s historic rainfall that hit the Bay Area, which brought 3.2 inches to San Francisco in two days. This week’s storm could bring roughly 1 to 1.5 inches to San Francisco between Tuesday afternoon and Wednesday afternoon  — still substantial and impactful because it’ll coincide with the king tides, Navarrete said. The king tides — influenced solely by the position of the moon and sun — are large because we’re near the peaks of what are known as the 18.6-year lunar node tidal cycle and the 4.4-year lunar perigee tidal cycle. Record-breaking ocean temperatures are also influencing the high sea levels, since hotter water takes up more volume. Southern California isn’t getting a major storm this week. Still, meteorologists warned that areas spared from hurricanes Marie and Rachel in early September and early October, and from high tides Oct. 27, could get hit with coastal flooding this week. In Orange and San Diego counties, forecasters with the National Weather Service warned of “extreme” risk from coastal flooding and high surf on Thanksgiving Day, and warned of “major” impacts from coastal flooding on Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday. Compared with the Oct. 27 coastal flooding — which damaged 114 homes and other structures in Huntington Beach alone, and also hit Newport Beach hard — this week’s flooding may be worse, forecasters warned. “It’ll most likely be at least as bad as that, and it could be a little worse because we are actually expecting a little bit of higher surf,” said Philip Gonsalves, meteorologist with the weather service office in San Diego, which also issues forecasts for Orange County. Makenna Cassidy and her husband, Jared, far left, join Otto Brown trying to bail out floodwater from their garage in the Sunset Beach area of Huntington Beach on Oct. 27. (Robert Gauthier / Los Angeles Times) With the maximum sea level possibly exceeding 8 feet on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thanksgiving Day, “this will bring widespread moderate-to-major coastal flooding,” the weather service’s San Diego office said. Newport Beach has been working to temporarily raise seawalls and build sand berms on beaches to prepare. Huntington Beach warned that low-lying roads will be closed Monday through Friday from 6 a.m. to 2 p.m. daily, including a total closure of a 3.7-mile stretch of Pacific Coast Highway through the neighborhood of Sunset Beach — from Seal Beach Boulevard to Warner Avenue. Huntington Beach also asked boaters to limit unnecessary travel through Huntington Harbour, since boat wakes — when tides are high — can “cause water to overtop seawalls and bulkheads, potentially flooding neighboring properties and damaging docks and private property.” In Los Angeles, Ventura, Santa Barbara and San Luis Obispo counties, there’s high confidence in record-breaking high tides, the weather service office in Oxnard said. The coastal flooding risk will be the highest on Wednesday and Thursday, exacerbated by elevated-to-high surf that peaks on those two days. With a swell coming from the west, west-facing beaches are at high risk, including the L.A. County coast from Santa Monica to the Palos Verdes Peninsula and the Ventura County coast from Faria Beach to Silver Strand Beach, including the inside of the harbors and Ventura Pier, according to meteorologist Dave Gomberg of the weather service’s Oxnard office. The swell won’t be as big in the Long Beach area, Gomberg said, but he’s still concerned about the high maximum sea levels for the area. Crews have been adding sand to the shoreline of the Long Beach Peninsula, which was hit hard by swells from the south from hurricanes Marie and  Rachel. “Visiting beaches is not advised,” especially on Wednesday and Thursday, the weather service’s Oxnard office said, despite how tempting  that might be on Thanksgiving, with air temperatures in Southern California forecast to be in the 70s. The shoreline “will be very wet at high tide. Sneaker waves are possible and occur without warning, washing much farther up the beach than expected,” the office said . Sand is added to the Long Beach Peninsula shoreline Oct. 26. (Robert Gauthier / Los Angeles Times) On the Central Coast, areas of greatest concern include Morro Bay, Pismo Beach, Oceano Dunes, Cayuco Pier, Avila Beach Pier and Pismo Beach Pier. Maximum sea level records could be broken yet again. On Oct. 27, the tide gauge in San Pedro broke a record, with the maximum sea level reaching 8.19 feet. A reasonable worst-case scenario for the maximum sea level on Wednesday in L.A. County would be up to 8.7 feet, the weather service said. The flooding that came in late October occurred even though there wasn’t significant surf. This time around, “we’ve got some larger surf,” which can worsen coastal flooding, said meteorologist Lisa Phillips of the National Weather Service in Oxnard. But there is some uncertainty. One factor that could result in lower-than-expected sea levels on Thanksgiving Day would be higher pressure moving over the area, which would “kind of squish the water down and may contribute to slightly lower levels of those tides,” weather service meteorologist Bryan Lewis said. Forecasters warned Sunday that the coastal threat could continue after this week. Another swell could threaten the Southern California coast starting again on the Sunday after Thanksgiving. articles.title: 台股杠杆退潮规模创30年之最，高盛下调评级并削减目标点位
articles.summary: 中国台湾股市正经历一场去杠杆风暴。上周五单日融资余额骤降490亿元台币，创下近30年最大单日降幅，高盛随即将台湾股市评级从"增持"下调至"中性"，并大幅削减目标点位。 中国台湾基准加权指数上周重挫17.5%，创1991年以来最大单周跌幅。周一指数反弹收涨2.16%，但市场情绪依然脆弱。 据彭博报道， 上市股票融资余额上周五单日大减490亿元台币（约15亿美元），创下彭博自1996年开始统计以来的单日最大降幅。融资余额目前已较10月创下的约6,530亿元台币纪录高点下降逾30%。 高盛驻香港策略师Alvin So在周六发布的研究报告中直言："散户杠杆已大幅下降，但追缴保证金和被迫去杠杆的风险仍然偏高。"他指出， 整体市场融资维持率已降至132%，接近130%的追缴保证金门槛，"目前已有53%的股票低于这一水平"。 高盛下调评级，目标点位大幅缩水 高盛在11月21日发布的报告中，将中国台湾在亚洲区域配置中的评级从"增持"（Overweight）下调至"中性"（Marketweight）， 并将2027年底加权指数目标点位从57,500点下调至50,000点。 以上周五指数水平约36,034点计算，50,000点的目标意味着约40%的潜在上涨空间，但高盛同时指出，当前台股40%的隐含波动率大幅压缩了风险调整后的回报吸引力。 报告写道："强劲的盈利增长（预计2027/2028年分别增长32%/25%）仍具支撑， 但AI资本支出风险、市场高度集中、相对估值溢价以及波动率居高不下，共同削弱了风险调整后的回报吸引力。" 高盛同时维持"优质科技股"作为核心持仓，并辅以"股息支撑的AI多元化配置"作为战术性补充。 外资持续净卖，散户逆势接盘 外资卖压是本轮下跌的核心驱动力。据高盛研报， 外资（QFII）上周净卖出台股现货58亿美元，其中台积电单周遭净卖出38亿美元。 年初至今，外资累计净卖出台股约950亿美元，台积电一只股票就占了约740亿美元。 与此同时，散户投资者逆势买入。 数据显示，ETF上周吸引约48亿美元净流入，其中宽基被动型ETF流入25亿美元，股息型ETF流入9亿美元，杠杆型及主动型ETF各流入约7亿美元。散户在融资大幅去化的同时，仍维持净买入姿态。 然而，散户的杠杆敞口依然不容忽视。数据显示，杠杆ETF规模仍高达110亿美元，占市场自由流通股的0.8%。Alvin So在报告中警告，这一敞口在市场持续下跌的情况下，仍构成潜在的被迫去杠杆风险。 卖空限制层层加码 面对持续下跌，中国台湾本月已三度收紧卖空规则。 中国台湾周六宣布，全面禁止低于前一交易日收盘价的卖空操作，涵盖融券卖空及借券卖空，新规于11月23日起生效。这是本月第三次出台卖空限制措施。 此前，已于11月9日将借券卖空的日内上限从30%下调至3%（以30日平均成交量为基准），并将融券保证金要求从90%提高至130%。11月20日再度收紧，将上限进一步压缩至1%，并规定当日跌幅超过3.5%的股票，次日不得在前收盘价以下卖空。最新措施还将融券保证金要求进一步提高至150%，并暂停受理证券商申请上市新认沽权证。 盈利基本面尚稳，但估值溢价制约空间 高盛研报指出，台股盈利基本面仍具支撑。中国台湾第三季度整体盈利同比增长71%，2027年预期每股盈利共识上调0.3%。科技板块预计在2027/2028年分别实现32%/25%的盈利增长。 然而，估值层面的压力不容忽视。数据显示，MSCI台湾指数当前12个月远期市盈率为12.7倍（低于历史均值1.3个标准差），24个月远期市盈率为10.0倍（低于历史均值2.2个标准差）。尽管绝对估值已有所回落，但台湾科技股相对全球科技同业仍存在21%的市盈率溢价（剔除台积电后为15%），处于历史高位，限制了其在全球配置中的相对吸引力。 报告同时指出， 科技板块在中国台湾整体盈利中的占比已从2010年代初的约50%升至2027年预期的约85% ，使台股对AI及半导体基本面的敏感度大幅提升。 散户杠杆与外资持仓双高，去化压力犹存 高盛研报揭示了当前市场结构的深层矛盾：外资大规模卖出的同时，散户和ETF持续接盘，但双方的持仓均处于历史高位，去化压力尚未充分释放。 外资方面，尽管年初至今已净卖出约950亿美元，外资在台积电的持股比例仍高达69%，在其他科技股的持股比例也维持在46%左右。该行指出，对冲基金仍大幅超配亚洲信息科技板块，若AI不确定性和市场波动持续，存在进一步减仓空间。 散户方面，融资余额虽已从280亿美元峰值降至170亿美元，但杠杆ETF规模仍高达110亿美元。该行警告，53%的股票融资维持率已低于130%的追缴保证金门槛，代表市场自由流通股（剔除台积电）的44%，"融资去化风险具有广泛性"。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: OpenAI又想叫暂停
articles.summary: 模型能力越强，讨论“暂缓”的声音就越多。 美国当地时间11月22日，OpenAI首席科学家雅库布·帕乔茨基（Jakub Pachocki）发表了题为《Perplexity and Intelligence》（困惑度与智能）的文字，公开公司内部追踪多年的预训练数据，并提出建立AI行业共同标准。 帕乔茨基希望各家前沿模型公司使用统一指标衡量模型能力，在安全监控能力达到要求之前，不突破约定的能力门槛。 这项提议也得到了OpenAI CEO山姆·奥特曼（Sam Altman）的支持。 01 一个与智能有关的数字 帕乔茨基这篇文章的核心，是所谓的“困惑度”（Perplexity）。 帕乔茨基将模型预测token的机制称为训练一个压缩器（Compressor）——模型从数据中提取规律，用更少的信息准确预测接下来会发生什么。困惑度衡量的就是这种预测能力。 模型预测得越准确，困惑度越低 。OpenAI实际公布的是对数困惑度，也就是交叉熵损失（Cross-Entropy Loss），数值同样是越低越好。 按照帕乔茨基公布的内部数据， GPT-3.5的对数困惑度约为0.99，GPT-4约为0.91 。前者已经能够支持流畅的对话，后者则开始有效利用思维链（Chain of Thought，CoT）进行推理。到了 最新阶段的GPT-6版本之后，困惑度指标已降至0.8以下 。 帕乔茨基表示，模型在数学、网络安全等领域开始表现出新的能力。其中一个 变化发生在对数困惑度降至约0.76——研究人员发现，在这个节点上模型开始连续解决一些具有挑战性的数学问题。 帕乔茨基提到，研究人员曾经在Slack中看到模型接连解决自己思考多年的问题。这些表现并非针对某一道题进行专门训练，而是模型底层能力提升后出现的结果。 帕乔茨基强调，这也是他重视困惑度的原因。 关键原因在于，这项数值不与模型能否完成任务直接关联，而是反映它从训练数据中学习信息的能力发生了什么变化。 我们过去经常讨论智能涌现， 困惑度持续下降带来的能力进化，就可以理解为一种涌现。 02 2027年助力预训练突破 以往，模型训练方法主要由人类研究人员提出，再通过大量实验验证。AI开始参与研究后，情况可能发生变化：模型不仅执行研究人员安排的任务，还可能帮助寻找新的算法、提出实验方案，甚至对训练方法本身作出贡献。 他预计，最早到2027年AI就可能在预训练领域取得一系列基础性进展。最新模型已经开始在研发过程中提供实质性的设计贡献。 帕乔茨基透露，OpenAI今年已经观察到预训练损失下降速度明显加快。不过，他也特别说明，现阶段主要来自长期研究和算力投入，AI自动化目前只贡献了较小部分。 帕乔茨基还预计， 随着对数困惑度进一步降至0.68至0.70，模型可能展现出目前尚无法预见的新能力。 不过，把困惑度作为共同标准，并不意味着问题已经解决。 帕乔茨基也承认，这一指标存在局限。 首先，各家公司的训练数据、数据配比和评估集不同，困惑度并不能直接用于横向比较。其次，困惑度不能直接衡量模型在具体任务中的表现。一个模型的预测能力提高，不代表它在所有数学、编程和安全测试中都会同步进步。此外，思维链推理等后训练技术也会改变模型能力，却不一定直接反映在预训练困惑度上。 还有一个关键问题：困惑度存在理论下限。 随着模型越来越接近训练数据所包含的信息熵，损失下降可能逐渐放缓。但这不代表能力提升也会停止。即使指标只发生很小的变化，也可能对应新的能力突破。 因此，帕乔茨基并不主张只用困惑度判断模型是否安全，而是希望把它与其他指标结合起来，形成一套共同标准。为了推动这项工作，OpenAI愿意公开更多预训练进展。 帕乔茨基认为，前沿模型公司应该共享必要的透明度信息 ，共同评估模型能力，并在红队测试和安全标准方面开展合作。 03 OpenAI与Closed AI 帕乔茨基发表文章后，奥特曼很快公开表态支持。“最近一段时间发布的最重要的事情。”奥特曼说。 奥特曼表示，OpenAI正在提高预训练进展的透明度，希望能够与其他公司以合作伙伴的身份，就共同限制达成一致。在他看来，这 不仅有助于确保AI安全和可控，也能推动整个行业建立共同规则。 对于帕乔茨基提出的困惑度限制，奥特曼也表示赞同。他希望各家实验室围绕困惑度及其他测量指标建立共同约束，在研究人员真正具备理解和监控AI行为的能力之前，不跨越预先设定的能力门槛。 他举出的例子，是开发下一代思维链监控器（CoT Monitors）。 在他看来，行业应该先明确第一道能力限制，再约定突破这道限制之前必须完成哪些安全工作。 不过，奥特曼的支持，并没有消除外界的疑虑。首先受到质疑的是OpenAI推动行业共同设限的动机。 一些网友认为， OpenAI此时强调行业限制和安全标准，是否也有为自身模型竞争力争取时间的考虑。 有人认为，这些说法更像是模型发布不及竞争对手时使用的理由。 还有人讽刺奥特曼频繁使用“透明度”一词，称 如果OpenAI真的希望提高透明度，就应该开源 ，而不是继续忽视用户对模型连续性的要求。 批评还涉及OpenAI的公司定位。 有网友直接建议将OpenAI改名为ClosedAI，认为公司 目前的开放程度已经配不上这个名字 。 本文来源： 腾讯科技 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 人形机器人最缺的，可能不是一双手，而是一张皮肤
articles.summary: 人形机器人正在变得越来越像人，但要真正走进工厂和家庭，仅仅拥有灵活的双手和敏捷的双腿还远远不够。触觉，可能是下一场技术进化的关键。 从一层柔软的仿生皮肤，到能够感知压力、摩擦甚至物体滑移的电子皮肤，一条新的产业链正在浮出水面。 一、发生了什么？——机器人开始学习触摸世界 1、机器人会跑会跳，为什么还拿不好一只杯子？ 2026年，人形机器人的运动能力不断突破。从奔跑、跳跃、复杂舞蹈，到工厂中的搬运与分拣，越来越多的机器人开始展示接近人类的动作技巧。人工智能模型也持续提升机器理解指令、识别环境和规划动作的能力。然而，当机器人真正走进工厂和家庭，许多看似普通的任务仍难以完成：它能识别桌上的杯子，却未必能稳稳拿起；可以完成复杂的舞蹈，却可能在整理衣物、摆放餐具和精密装配时频繁失误。 原因之一在于触觉。人类拿起盛满水的纸杯，会持续感知杯壁形变、接触面摩擦和轻微滑动，并在不经意间调整握力。摄像头能判断物体的位置和外形，却难以直接获取接触面受力；机械臂上的六维力传感器可以测量整体受力，却不能完整还原每根手指、每个接触点的压力分布。物体一旦被遮挡，或发生视觉难以识别的滑移，缺乏局部触觉反馈就会影响操作稳定性。 电子皮肤正是围绕这一缺口发展起来的技术。它将柔性基材、敏感功能材料、电极和读取电路集成在可贴附的结构中，通过大量触觉单元获取接触、压力和形变信息。 ……

articles.title: 市场已定价“AI基建周期2027年见顶”，摩根大通：基本面不支持“极度悲观”的市场预期
articles.summary: 摩根大通认为，亚洲科技硬件股近期的暴跌，已提前计入了市场对“未来3-4个月EPS下修25%-30%及2027年盈利见顶”的极度悲观预期，但若悲观预期落空，科技股有望迎来20%以上的强劲反弹。 追风交易台消息，11月22日，摩根大通Gokul Hariharan团队研报指出，自9月初以来亚洲科技股累计下跌超过30%，而同期MSCI亚太指数跌幅为15%-20%，投资者讨论的焦点已从“2028年是否见顶”转向“2027年是否就是峰值”。 (亚洲科技板块除存储外的估值已回落至平均市盈率水平) 摩根大通认为，市场当前的定价隐含了未来3-4个月25%-30%的紧急盈利下修。但该行预计， 实际EPS下修幅度仅为5%-10% ，且行业供需缺口仍高达25%-30%。 一旦市场担忧的上述深度下滑未能发生 ， 科技股有望迎来20%以上的强劲反弹 。 研报同时指出，科技股若要开启更强劲的上涨，必须看到AI模型催生出全新的应用场景，并打开新的市场空间（TAM） 。类似2025年11月“Claude Code时刻”（AI编程爆发）那样的破圈效应。 目前市场仅看到一些间接信号：头部AI实验室正将更大比例的算力（Token）预算重新倾斜至模型训练，显示出AI规模化法则（Scaling Law）仍在加速。不过，在看到更明确的商业化落地证据前，市场暂不会为此提前定价。 供应链ROI仍健康，市场情绪与基本面出现背离 摩根大通认为，当前股价已经在按“AI基础设施资本开支2027年见顶、此后显著下滑”来交易，但AI产业链的证据并不支持这一判断。 硬件厂商、公有云厂商与模型厂商的单位经济效益均相当健康，投资意愿也未见下降。 （亚洲科技板块远期市净率已大幅回落，但净资产收益率ROE仍攀升至约40%的历史高位） 真正需要观察的是，极端悲观的市场情绪与近期多重限制——包括利率上行导致的融资受限、芯片销售限制等是否会在AI基础设施需求端引发连锁反应。 该行列出四个可能改变其偏乐观判断的观测点 ： 一是 针对AI训练与模型进步的监管压力，毕竟当前token支出大部分投向训练； 二是 新云服务公司融资问题与美国出口芯片限制引发算力定价崩塌、需求冻结； 三是 超大规模云厂商与AI实验室因新新的市场空间（TAM）迟迟未现而暂停资本开支； 四是 半导体与硬件产业链出现库存积压迹象。 总体而言，该行更关注token需求的驱动因素，认为只要需求保持强劲，数据中心容量等供给侧问题会自行解决。 BIS新规短期压制10%-12%算力需求，长期难扼杀需求 美国商务部工业与安全局（BIS）推出的最新出口管制新规，将禁止芯片厂商在未获许可的情况下，向东南亚云服务商销售高性能GPU。 摩根大通估算，这可能短期压制15%-20%的GPU需求，对应整体AI算力需求受影响约10%-12%，因此初期的订单下调在所难免。 但该行认为需求依然存在。 报告提到，芯片厂商，如Google TPU、AMD正试图承接可能被腾出的产能，这应使 供需在2027年前保持紧平衡。 值得注意的是，在供给端的上游环节，订单下调可能来得更慢。 云厂商2027年资本开支预期不变 摩根大通美国研究团队预测，超大规模云厂商合计资本开支2027年同比增长87%，2028年增长19%。 该行称， 目前尚未从主要超大规模云厂商或大型新云服务商处发现任何放缓支出的信号。 受数据中心不确定性影响， 部分项目可能从2027年小幅推迟至2028年，但整体增长态势预计延续至2028年。 新云服务商调整有限，再签约价格反而更高 远程访问限制是否引发新云服务商严重供过于求，是摩根大通眼中最关键的观察领域之一。 目前该行仅观察到部分新云服务商小规模调整，但算力定价并未出现普遍性下跌，释放出的供给也被强劲需求迅速吸收。 更值得关注的是，部分合同再签约的每GPU价格反而更高，原因是许多合约签订于2025年末或2026年初，当时算力价格远低于现在。 不过该行提醒，若算力需求与GPU租赁价格出现系统性下移，上游GPU订单将面临大幅下修的风险，这一领域仍需持续跟踪。 训练占比上升：ARR指标或低估真实算力需求 摩根大通在近3-4个月的研究中反复提示，多数AI实验室的训练算力占比在上升，大部分token仍分配于训练。 这与投资者传统认知，推理应占token支出比例越来越高形成反差。该行认为这有三重含义： 其一，ARR等仅衡量推理token或平台token消耗的传统指标，可能低估AI算力需求； 其二，训练占比上升或意味AI scaling law推进更快，有利于未来AI进展与新TAM出现； 其三，头部AI实验室的投资将继续激进，因为通往前沿的竞赛在加速——Meta、Google等在过去3-4个月正追赶前沿。 该行预计， 在模型能力快速迭代与AI对齐研究token支出增加的背景下，训练占比短期内将维持高位，同时推理token仍将高速增长。 2027年CoWoS对应34-36GW算力，与美国数据中心40GW增量匹配 根据台积电先进封装（CoWoS）的出货数据测算，2027年全球新增的AI芯片（含GPU与定制芯片ASIC）预计将带来约34至36吉瓦（GW）的净新增电力负荷。 这一数字与美国2027年数据中心新增40吉瓦装机容量的预期基本吻合，且尚未计入海外需求，而近期美国云巨头正加速向海外扩张数据中心。 若按各类AI芯片的满载功耗（TDP）上限测算，到2028年，这一新增算力功耗需求可能进一步攀升至50至53吉瓦。 摩根大通表示，美国中期选举后，本土数据中心的建设规划将如何演变仍需观察。 不过，由于海外市场仍有充足的数据中心装机与电力资源可供调配，科技行业仍有充足时间适应美国的政策变化。 而在当前股价水平下，市场已按云巨头资本开支将在“2027年见顶”而非“2028年见顶”进行了过度悲观的定价。 CPO进展或略放缓，开源模型不会削弱token需求驱动 关于黄仁勋离开英伟达是否放慢技术创新与CPO等新产品推出，摩根大通判断未来两年英伟达的产品路线图应大体不受影响。 近期供应链动作，安抚供应商、与基板、OSAT等关键供应商签署更多合约，显示其在未来12-24个月仍将保持供应链掌控力。 CPO是可能略有放缓的领域 ：一方面英伟达一直是主要推动者，而ASIC阵营态度较为冷淡；另一方面供应链仍复杂，存在实质性挑战需要克服。 与此同时，HVDC与3D封装预计进展不变，2028年将实现有意义的采用。2028年之后，则需等待新的管理团队在技术创新与供应链合作上的态度。 摩根大通认为，随着企业对开源模型的兴趣上升、垂直AI厂商需求增加，开源大语言模型的需求不太可能改变。 企业AI采用提速后，开源与专有前沿模型将针对不同工作负载各自获得强劲采用。 报告强调，鉴于开源模型需求强劲，未来6个月预计会出现接近前沿水平的非中国开源模型。中期看，开源模型不会实质性削弱其作为token需求增长关键驱动的地位。 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ 以上精彩内容来自 articles.title: 傲意科技完成数亿元D轮融资，年内第二轮获国资产业资本加码
articles.summary: 11月23日，上海傲意信息科技有限公司（以下简称“傲意科技”）宣布完成数亿元D轮融资，由中兵顺景、长江资本、光谷产投等联合投资。 这是傲意科技2026年完成的第二轮融资。今年3月，公司完成1.5亿元C1轮融资，由中金资本旗下中金脑科学基金领投。本轮融资的具体金额与投后估值暂未披露。 本轮投资方特点是国资背景较密集。中兵顺景为中国兵器工业集团旗下产业投资平台，长江资本依托长江产业投资集团，光谷产投为武汉东湖高新区产业投资平台。 傲意科技董事、副总裁张琦表示，本轮融资将用于加速具身智能商业化进程。张琦还透露，公司目前正积极推进上市前的相关准备。 除灵巧手外，傲意科技也在拓展具身智能数据采集业务，公司称自主研发的EMG-EGO系统已与国内外多家产业链企业开展合作。 傲意科技与A股投资者直接相关的身份，是A股上市公司杭州雷迪克节能科技股份有限公司（以下简称“雷迪克”， 300652.SZ ）的参股公司。2025年11月，雷迪克公告拟以约1.6亿元对价，通过受让股权及增资方式合计取得傲意科技20.41%股权。 雷迪克2025年12月15日的进展公告显示，这笔交易已实施完毕，工商变更已办理完成，雷迪克由此成为仅次于创始人倪华良的第二大股东。 傲意科技成立于2015年，主营机器人灵巧手、多指夹爪等末端执行器，同时经营智能仿生手等脑机接口与康复产品。 公司称，产品服务全球近200家具身智能企业，在珠海运营自建工厂，具备万台级年产能。 从雷迪克此前披露的交易公告看，傲意科技2024年实现营业收入3107.75万元，归母净利润为-753.49万元，该年度数据经审计。 2025年上半年，傲意科技实现营业收入2495.34万元，归母净利润为-265.72万元，数据未经审计。此后未见更新的财务数据披露。 对雷迪克而言，傲意科技是公司从汽车轴承切入机器人零部件的支点之一。雷迪克2025年以来控股誊展精密、间接持有北方机械20%股权权益，布局丝杠环节。 2025年11月，傲意科技参与了雷迪克出资比例占9成的合资公司，作为关节模组与灵巧手模组总成的研发生产平台。 此外，雷迪克2026年半年度报告还将傲意科技列为参股公司。截至2026年6月末，公司对傲意科技的长期股权投资期末账面价值约1.6亿元。 雷迪克2026年7月的投资者关系活动记录显示，公司目前持有傲意科技20.10%股权，低于交易完成时公告的20.41%。 对这家灵巧手公司来说，更关键的验证在经营端。灵巧手赛道参与者增多、价格竞争加剧，结合已披露数据，公司收入规模尚小、此前尚未实现盈利。 从目前披露的信息看，本轮融资为傲意科技引入了新的国资背景投资方，具体交易结构与股权变化尚未披露。国资产业资本进入后，灵巧手与具身数据采集业务后续收入情况还需要长期观察。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: Manus联创张涛：免费补贴是AI应用创业的最大陷阱，要面向“六个月后的模型”做创新
articles.summary: 近日，Manus联合创始人、首席产品官张涛在北京大学AI创投课堂发表了一场长达两小时的演讲，披露了这家30人公司从0到1的创业决策链条。在这场演讲中，张涛抛出了一个在当前AI创业圈颇具争议的判断：免费补贴是AI应用创业最大的陷阱，中国AI创业者可能在被上一代移动互联网的打法所误导。 我觉得回看过去两三年，中国AI应用创业，我觉得有一个非常大的陷阱，就是我们被上一代移动互联网创业的免费补贴陷阱给迷惑了，以为这一代还要这么做，完全错误。 张涛在演讲中透露，Manus发布后第一个月的ARR（年度经常性收入）即突破4000万元人民币，接近5000万，核心用户中不乏每月在平台消费4000至5000美元的企业管理者。他将这一成绩归结于一个核心判断：在AI时代，让用户真实感受到智能，才是产品最重要的价值，而非靠补贴堆砌DAU。 砍掉7个月心血：一个关于时间成本的战略判断 在Manus诞生之前，有一段鲜为人知的弯路。 2024年3月，张涛与联合创始人、首席科学家Pick加入肖弘（Red）的团队后，团队的第一个方向并非Agent，而是一款AI原生浏览器。逻辑顺理成章：公司此前的产品Monica是浏览器插件，天花板明显，"做浏览器插件出身的公司，很容易推演到下一个产品应该做个浏览器"。 这款浏览器做了整整7个月，到2024年10月已接近发布状态。张涛坦言，"发出来应该对市场还是有点惊艳的"。但肖弘最终拍板将其sunset（放弃）。 核心原因有两个。其一，产品体验的嫁接困境：所有人拿到AI浏览器后，第一个问题都是"我在Chrome里用的功能，在你这里去哪找"，用户永远用旧体验的基准线来衡量新产品，而创业团队根本无力在浏览器基础功能上对齐苹果和Google。其二，时间成本的判断：一旦发布，团队将被迫在这个方向上耗费3至6个月，而"如果你在创业，钱是最不值钱的东西，浪费了时间才是最可怕的"。 张涛事后评价，这是Manus历史上最重要的一个决定，"如果当时不是因为sunset了那个浏览器产品，就没有后来的Manus"。 看见拐点：从Cursor里读出的不是Coding机会 2024年7月，Cursor爆火。市场上随即涌现出大量Coding Agent的跟随者。张涛和Pick看到的却是另一件事。 "我们发现Sonnet 3.5 V2解锁的不是单纯的Coding能力，而是一个agentic能力。"张涛说，这包括两个维度：Long Horizon Planning（长程规划）——模型开始主动将任务拆解为多步骤，而非在单轮对话中强行完成；以及大幅增强的Tool Use（工具调用）能力。 在张涛看来，这个能力解锁的对象不是工程师，而是普通人。"这个世界不需要更多的engineer了，而且engineer也不需要更多fancy的工具了。"他们看到的机会是：通过Coding作为中介，去解决普通用户的通用场景问题。 2024年12月，Manus正式立项。两个半月后，2025年3月5日发布。发布当天，张涛才发现，"好像全世界只有我们在做这个，大家都还是在做Coding"。 这背后有一套Pick一直坚持的架构哲学，张涛将其概括为"Less structure, more intelligence"：Manus的Honeycomb架构从第一版起就完全抛弃了workflow，每一步的思考和决策全部交由模型自主决定，"不管你让Manus做research、做slides、做网站、写数据分析，所有的事情都是Manus自己决定下一步干什么的"。 这个赌注在2025年2月中旬Anthropic发布Claude 3.7的当晚得到验证。张涛在即刻发文"信仰充值的一晚"——Honeycomb一行代码未改，仅将模型endpoint从3.5 V2切换至3.7，benchmark上剩余未解决的问题"百分之二三十，全部一下就解了"。 反对“互联网式烧钱”：免费补贴是AI创业最大的陷阱 Manus发布时，连付费功能都没有做。 3月5日上线，发现火爆程度超出预期，团队才从零开始搭建定价体系，到3月20多号才上线付费功能。 而在这中间，邀请码成了救命稻草。原因极为现实：公司账上只剩八九百万美元，在有邀请码限制的情况下，单日最高烧掉50万美元。"如果没有邀请码，我们公司从3月5号发布，可能就一撑一个星期，3月12号就可以关门了。" 但张涛想说的不只是这段险情，而是一个更根本的判断： AI时代，免费补贴是错误方向。 我觉得回看过去两三年，中国AI应用创业有一个非常大的陷阱，就是我们被上一代移动互联网创业的免费补贴陷阱给迷惑了，以为这一代还要这么做，完全错误。 为什么？因为AI这个时代，智能本身，如果说你的performance本身是足够好的，一定会有人愿意付费的，一定是有人愿意付费的。 他的逻辑是：免费补贴吸引来的是无效用户，这些用户的反馈会迷惑创业者的注意力； 而付费用户是用钱投票的用户，他们的需求才是真实需求。"你围绕那个需求去做，你就能吸引更多愿意付费的人。" 他还特别点出大厂的困境：上线第一天拿一两千万预算补贴用户，有了一二十万DAU之后，没有人敢在第二个月转向收费，"它就一直拖累了你对于真实用户市场的感知能力"。 Manus目前最满意且付费最多的用户群体，是企业管理者——CEO、小老板、部门主管。张涛的解释直接："General AI Agent，General通用，在公司里面谁的屁事最多？老板嘛。" 下一个转折点在哪里：面向“6个月后的模型” 张涛在演讲中给出了一个具体的创业方向预判， 他称之为"1秒钟延迟的Sora时刻"。 "我一直在等待一个时刻，就是从你输出prompt到你看到画面延迟小于1秒钟。我觉得当这个turning point到来的时候，会是这一轮AI整个应用创业非常重要的转折点。" 他的判断是，1秒延迟的视频生成模型已经不是视频生成模型， "它就是新一代的操作系统" 。届时的交互方式将从单向内容消费变为每个人自主参与的互动创作，"它已经不是单纯的一人制作、多人消费了"。他认为这一时刻"6个月之内一定会发生"，并鼓励创业者现在就开始围绕这个方向准备产品形态。 这一判断背后，是张涛对AI创业方法论的一贯主张：永远面向6个月后的模型外溢能力去创新，而不是基于今天的模型能力修修补补。"你应该想象的是6个月之后模型会变成什么样子。如果6个月之后模型是那个样子，我会用什么样的产品形态去匹配那个时候的模型。" 他同时强调，坚持做General（通用）是Manus的另一个关键战略判断。"品牌心智的认知是很难花钱去买的，你在用户心中的Mindset，是花几亿美金都很难改变的事情。"正因为一开始占住了"什么都能干"的心智，Manus在后续推出WebDev、Slides、Video等子功能时都顺理成章，而那些从垂直场景起家的竞品，想转向通用任务时则面临用户认知的强烈阻力。 在资本效率问题上，张涛透露，Manus做到20亿美元估值时，历史上总共花掉的融资额约为5000至6000万美元。"我们团队可能是国内AI startup里资本利用效率最高的一支团队。"他的结论是：AI创业与其他创业没有本质区别，"不是因为加了个AI的定语，你就可以很理所当然地亏钱"。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 铠侠暴跌之后，高盛认为：估值偏低而股东回报强劲，“与过去的航运股类似”
articles.summary: 铠侠控股股价近期大幅下挫，但高盛认为进一步下行空间有限，并维持买入评级。 追风交易台消息，11月22日，高盛分析师Shuhei Nakamura与Kaho Otake发布研究报告指出，铠侠股价当前对应截至2028年3月的财年， 预期市盈率仅约1.5倍，市净率在不考虑额外回购的情形下亦低于1倍，均处于历史周期低位。 与此同时，公司管理层已承诺将100%的超额自由现金流返还股东， 高盛测算截至2028年3月的财年及截至2029年3月的财年的总股东回报率将分别超过30%和约50%。 高盛下调了铠侠截至2028年3月的财年至截至2029年3月的财年的营业利润预测，降幅分别为15%和30% ，主要反映2028年NAND供需趋于平衡的预判，但因预计公司将加大股票回购力度， 每股收益预测的修正幅度相对温和，分别仅为-2%和-4%。 供需格局：2028年或迎来拐点 高盛全球团队最新研究显示，数据中心NAND需求前景有所改善，但PC及智能手机等消费类应用需求持续疲软。 与此同时，以中国厂商为核心的供给端扩张加快，导致高盛判断： 尽管NAND市场供需偏紧的格局有望延续至2026至2027年，但2028年供需有可能逐步趋于平衡。 基于上述判断，高盛在模型中新增了一项假设—— 铠侠NAND均价将从2027年4至6月起温和下滑，预计2028日历年度价格跌幅略超20%。 这一调整导致截至2028年3月的财年和截至2029年3月的财年营业利润预测分别下调15%和30%，截至2027年3月的财年预测维持不变。 高盛预计，铠侠截至2028年3月的财年和截至2029年3月的财年的营业利润，仍可分别维持在约10.2万亿日元和9.9万亿日元的高位，对应营业利润率分别约为82%和80%。 报告强调，若2028年AI资本支出增速归零，截至2029年3月的财年营业利润将较基准情景下降约22%；若AI资本支出同比下降10%，降幅则可能扩大至约52%。 估值：已计入悲观预期，历史底部特征明显 高盛指出，从历史经验来看，存储芯片股在周期峰值时对应的市盈率通常为3至4倍，周期中段则在高个位数至约10倍之间。而铠侠当前约1.5倍的2028年3月的财年预期市盈率，意味着市场已计入了相当程度的悲观预期。 从市净率角度来看，高盛测算，若不考虑额外回购，铠侠2028年3月的财年末每股账面价值约为9,120日元，对应市净率同样低于1倍。 高盛援引历史数据指出， 主要存储芯片厂商的股价在过去均于市净率接近1倍时出现反弹，这一水平构成较强的估值支撑。 鉴于此，高盛将估值基准年从2027年3月的财年至2028年3月的财年的平均值上调至2028年3月的财年单一年度，并将参照同业组合得出的权益资本成本（Cost of Equity）假设从20%上调至30%，目标价对应2028年3月的财年预期市盈率为4倍。 股东回报：股东总回报或超30%，类比历史航运股 高盛认为，强劲的股东回报是推动铠侠股价修复的关键催化剂。 铠侠管理层在2Q业绩发布时宣布，将把100%的超额自由现金流返还股东。 高盛以"现金及存款相当于至少三个月销售额"作为超额现金的界定标准进行测算， 预计铠侠2028财年的股票回购规模可达约3.5万亿日元，2029财年进一步升至约6.2万亿日元，叠加股息后，股东总回报收益率分别超过30%和约50%。 高盛在报告中特别提及，铠侠与过去的航运股具有相似之处。 即便市场行情见顶，持续的高额股东回报依然有望支撑股价及估值倍数上行。 报告同时指出，股价的近期下跌实际上使公司在执行未来回购计划时，能够以更低价格购回更多股份，从而提升每股回报，这一效应已部分反映在高盛对EPS的修正幅度相对温和的处理中。 在股息层面，高盛预测铠侠2027年3月的财年至2029年3月的财年每股股息分别为300日元、450日元和600日元，呈逐年提升趋势。 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ 以上精彩内容来自 追风交易台 。 更详细的解读，包括实时解读、一线研究等内容，请加入【 追风交易台▪年度会员 】 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
